newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton called to open 0.20 cent lower.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton called to open 0.20 cent lower.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures were called to open 0.20 cent lower Thursday, based on market orders at 1018 EDT, traders said.
USDA put new sales for the week ended July 3 at a light 33,800 480-lb bales in the 1997/98 season.
Accumulated shipments in the 1996/97 season reached 6.218 million bales out of the USDA's estimate of 6.8 million bales.
Floor sources viewed the report as slightly negative for prices.
Wednesday, most-active December closed 0.19 cent firmer at 74.35 cents a lb, traded 74.55 to 74.15 cents. The rest ended unchanged to 0.44 cent higher.
An estimated 12,000 lots changed hands on the day.
Support remained at the contract low of 73.70 cents followed by 70.00 cents for December delivery, with resistance at 75.00 cents followed by 76.00 cents.
NYCE said 63 notices were issued today, bringing the total to 841 notices issued to date.
